title: land pushes only through the kb's kbgit.py sync and lanes every project by kblane, so a host project of the plugin cannot land an item (second-project run)
goal: A host project of the plugin lands an item: land's push step runs the argv of a new backlog.json setting land_push (default the kb's kbgit.py sync --push, so the kb's landings are unchanged; a host names e.g. git push origin HEAD:main), and lane_module accepts an empty value meaning no code lane, so every commit lands as content (done --commit, then the push); the plugin's sprint skill names land_push where it pushes the claims; backlog.py config prints both; the gates on the push setting and the empty lane are answered before code

gates.question: How does land push in a project with no _tools/kbgit.py?
options: setting: a backlog.json land_push argv list, run from the project root like land_stale (a .py first element runs under python3), default ["_tools/kbgit.py", "sync", "--push"] so the kb is unchanged; a host names its own push, e.g. ["git", "push", "origin", "HEAD:main"]
detect: land runs kbgit.py sync --push when the project has _tools/kbgit.py, else a plain git push of HEAD to the integration remote's main

gates.question: How does a project say it has no code lane?
options: empty: lane_module accepts an empty string, meaning no code lane: every commit lands as content (done --commit, then land_push), and unlanded_code reads nothing
module: the plugin ships a nolane module whose paths_lane calls every path content, and a host names it in lane_module
